f Y=2 Y=4
X=1 14 18
X=3 12 18

Compute P(X=3|Y=2) given that the discrete random variables X and Y have the joint probability mass function f(x,y) shown in the table above.

a
14
b
34
c
13
d
23
e
12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by P(X=3|Y=2)=P(X=3,Y=2)P(Y=2)=f(3,2)fY(2), where f(x,y) is the joint probability mass function of X and Y, and fY(y) is the marginal distribution of Y.

Recall that the marginal distribution for Y corresponds to the column totals. Thus, fY(2)=f(1,2)+f(3,2)=14+12=34.

From the given table, we have that f(3,2)=12.

Finally, substituting fY(2)=34 and f(3,2)=12 in our formula above, we obtain P(X=3|Y=2)=f(3,2)fY(2)=(12)(34)=23.
